newsitem.title: UK: SWIMMING-BANNED LU RETURNS WITH WORLD CUP WIN.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-BANNED LU RETURNS WITH WORLD CUP WIN.

text.p: Chinese world champion Lu Bin made a winning return to competition abroad on Tuesday after serving a two-year doping ban.
Lu was one of seven Chinese swimmers who tested positive at the October 1994 Asian Games in Hiroshima and were banned for two years.
She trained throughout her suspension and returned to international competition in the Beijing leg of the eight-venue World Cup series earlier this month.
She managed just two fifth places and one sixth in Beijing but on Tuesday celebrated victory in her first appearance in Europe since her triumphs of the 1994 world championships in Rome.

Lu, 20 earlier this month, won the 50 metres backstroke in 28.74 seconds, seizing the lead with a long underwater start and holding off French challenger Anne-Francoise Glatre on the return length of Glasgow's new Tollcross Park pool.
Lu had earlier failed to make the final of the 200 metres backstroke but backstroke is not her speciality and she is using it to feel her way back into competition before resuming her main events.

Lu made a spectacular mark in the 1994 world championships as a 17-year-old, winning the 200 individual medley, sharing in two Chinese relay victories and taking silver medals in the 100 and 200 freestyle.
In the Asian Games in Hiroshima a month later she obliterated the 200 individual medley world record but the time was annulled after the positve dope test.
She has always denied taking drugs and suggests her sample might have been tampered with.
"One thing is for sure. I never took any drugs," she said, her words translated by a Chinese team official, after Tuesday's victory.
"I'd like to show that I have this ability to give good performance in competition. I want to show I had something in my mind to keep training very hard for the last two years."
Lu was one of three Chinese winners on the first day of the two-day meeting, fifth leg of the World Cup series in 25-metre pools.
Liu Limin, 100 and 200 metres butterfly gold medallist at the 1994 world championships, swam the second-fastest time in the world this season to race away in the 100 butterfly in 58.42.
Han Xue, short-course 50 breaststroke world record holder, scored a similarly emphatic win in the women's 100 metres breaststroke.
But compatriot Chao Na was pipped by former East German Katrin Meissner in the women's 50 metres freestyle.
Australia were the day's most prolific winners, with Michael Klim repeating the double he achieved last Saturday in Malmo by winning the 100 freestyle and 50 butterfly.

Klim repeated his Malmo time of 48.86 in the 100 freestyle and finished powerfully in the butterfly sprint to overhaul Britain's Mark Foster, holder of the world best time in the event, and win by 0.08 of a econds in 23.92.

Fourteen-year-old Natasha Bowron claimed another golden Australian double by winning the women's 200 and 800 freestyle and there were also wins for Adrian Radley (100 backstroke) and Matthew Dunn (400 individual medley).
